turnaround_reason: Stock is down ~70% from its 2022 peak as Starlink's vertically-integrated, lower-cost aviation Wi-Fi push structurally erodes Gogo's legacy business aviation connectivity moat, with revenue basically flat-to-down and a heavy debt load left over from the pre-LEO-competition era.
bullish_points: Won a 5-year sole-source federal government satcom contract and got FAA/EASA certification for its own LEO-based Galileo system (300+ antennas shipped, 99 activations, 31 STCs done with 20 more expected in H1 2026)
Acquired Satcom Direct (~$375M cash + 5M shares) to bulk up scale and product breadth against Starlink rather than cede the market passively
Forward PE of only 4.9x if FY2026 guidance ($922M revenue, $0.67 EPS) holds — priced for continued decline, not for stabilization
EV/EBITDA of 7.2x is not demanding for a business still generating positive FCF ($24.5M) and operating cash flow ($84.8M)
Director bought 250k shares in the open market in March 2026 around $4.54-4.57 — a real insider bet near current levels
bearish_points: Total debt of ~$903M against a $531M market cap is a genuinely dangerous leverage profile for a company facing a structural competitive threat, not a cyclical one
Starlink is vertically integrated (owns the satellites) and undercutting on price — Gogo can certify more STCs but can't out-cost SpaceX's economics
Revenue growth is negative (-1.7% ttm) even before accounting for the dilutive Satcom Direct deal financing
Only 2 analysts cover the name and neither issued a strong buy — thin coverage means limited independent validation of the bull case
Q1 2026 revenue missed estimates ($226.3M vs $233.3M) even as EPS beat, suggesting the top-line erosion is already showing up
catalyst: Q2 earnings — first look at whether Galileo/LEO STC ramp and the Satcom Direct integration are offsetting legacy revenue erosion
suggested_trade: Skip, or at most a small spot position sized for the leverage risk — not an options trade given the binary structural threat from Starlink
key_risk: Starlink continues taking business aviation share faster than Gogo's LEO buildout can offset, and the debt load leaves no room for a slow bleed
would_skip_if: Q2 shows legacy revenue erosion accelerating rather than being offset by Galileo/Satcom Direct contribution, or any sign of covenant/refinancing stress
